tagline: From Lanesborough farmland to the top of Massachusetts and down again.
intro: From open farmland in Lanesborough the parkway climbs through Mount Greylock State Reservation to the 3,491-foot summit, the state's high point, then comes down the Notch Road to North Adams. The climb runs from northern hardwoods to balsam fir and red spruce, like going from Pennsylvania to northern Maine in under an hour.

Cars came early. A pair of steam-powered Locomobiles made the summit by the Notch Road in 1902, and a road from the south followed in 1907. Herman Melville could see the mountain from his house in Pittsfield and dedicated a novel to it.

moments.title: Mount Greylock summit
moments.text: A circular staircase climbs the 93-foot War Memorial Tower for views across western New England into New York, beside the stone and wood Bascom Lodge the CCC built.

moments.title: Thunderbolt Ski Trail
moments.text: The CCC cut this trail in 1934 to drop 2,000 feet from the summit in just under two miles, and championship downhill races ran on it through the late 1950s.

moments.title: North Adams
moments.text: At the byway's northern end a heritage state park tells how the Hoosac Tunnel was built, and the old Sprague Electric plant became a museum of contemporary art in 1999.

practical: The parkway through the reservation is open to cars from late May through mid-October. The 70 miles of trails stay open all year.
